reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh independent audit instance
findings: Receipt SHA-256, canonical fingerprint, implementation digest, both implementation-file hashes and all 25 provenance-input hashes and byte sizes independently match. Fresh reconstruction reproduces the 30 ordered structured prompts and semantic SHA-256 1bfcf40b0f25e118161e24e05e3cdec351bd1aede2b81b7717558f622033ceb3.

The 60 bound rows form complete 30-case MTP and 30-case hybrid arms with no duplicate or missing keys and exact prompt equality to the frozen generator. Every response binds model alias fable-tc-l1.0, the MTP arm advertises none,draft-mtp, the hybrid arm advertises none,draft-mtp,ngram-cache, and both arms use the frozen 128-token greedy request controls. The service evidence binds the same binary/model hashes and restored path/argv.

Independent comparison reproduces 30/30 byte-exact response pairs and 30/30 hybrid requests with aggregate draft tokens. Both arms emit 3,840 tokens and every request reaches the frozen 128-token limit. MTP totals 3,042 drafted/3,030 accepted tokens; hybrid totals 4,619 drafted/2,928 accepted, reducing aggregate acceptance from 99.6055% to 63.3903%.

Independent wall aggregation reproduces 60.3294884 seconds for MTP, 87.5789771 seconds for hybrid, throughput 0.06365046516785457 versus 0.04384613896114296 tokens per millisecond and hybrid/MTP ratio 0.6888581072505122. The treatment is 45.17% slower, not 3x faster. Paired median speed ratio is 0.701754; only the first three of 30 hybrid cases are faster, and the best paired case is 1.103x, still far below the frozen threshold.

False-negative sensitivities make startup order and client overhead implausible explanations. Excluding the first one, two, four or eight fresh-treatment cases lowers the wall ratio to 0.6801, 0.6719, 0.6538 and 0.6466. Response-reported server generation time yields an even lower 0.603325 ratio, and prompt-plus-generation server time yields 0.675649. Thus cold launch, first-request warmup and client timing cannot rescue the performance gate.

The attribution failure is also independently confirmed. Exhaustive recursive inspection of every bound response finds only aggregate draft_n/draft_n_accepted and the advertised speculative.types string; the bound exported metrics contain no speculative, ngram, MTP, draft or acceptance series. The larger hybrid draft count suggests additional proposer activity but cannot establish which proposer supplied or accepted any token, so the historical 31.64% n-gram share remains unobservable and must not be inferred.

The predecessor's synthetic 3x result used autoregressive verification steps as its baseline, while this successor preregistered a materially different and stricter 3x wall-throughput gate against active physical MTP. Consequently this rejection falsifies the live R1 hypothesis and confirms that transplanting the synthetic 3x number as incremental live-over-MTP qualification was a false positive; it does not refute the simulator's internal arithmetic or measure live hybrid versus pure autoregression.

Exact parity, route advertisement, draft coverage, restoration and endpoint health pass, but the all-gates conjunction fails decisively on speed and proposer attribution. The claim is bounded to this binary/model, frozen structured prompts, sequential four-slot route and metric definitions; it makes no per-proposer share, model-forward reduction, production, pure-autoregressive comparison or out-of-panel claim.
